The game was surprisingly shorter than I had expected it to be. It took me  about 3 hours to complete. At first the game and story were very engaging. I really enjoyed the idea of having access to pretty much all information and having the ability to do face and image scans from videos and photographs. However, it became a little less enjoyable as the actual storyline for the game kicked in pretty much full force when you meet the main character. You're then just forced to  jump through whatever hoops the game holds out in front of you whether you want or not. The investigation then becomes annoyingly predictable and the game becomes less fun. The way the trailer looked it seemed like you would be pretty busy and very involved in your workload, but you get maybe 2 work days of fun investigating. I'm honestly not sure if I would recommend this game at full price. I got it on sale for about $8 and would probably say it's worth about that if not less. This wouldve been so much cooler if there were more caseloads that didn't have anything to do with the story's 'hidden' agenda or just not as obvious about it. Even better if it had an completely separate option of play that was a set number of cases to try and solve just for fun. In the end, no, I don't think this is a good enough for $14. If you want it, get it on sale.

What a game! I went into this with zero expectations and came out amazed. 

This game is incredibly written, the puzzles, the story, the characters. It is all genuinely incredible. The one thing I like about this game is that you feel immersed into the experience, it feels very real and you feel as if real lives are at stake. 

The cases are somewhat predictable, but not fully, there was times I was questioning myself and what to do. At some point I genuinely felt panic. It is very hard not to love this game, the sound design to the style of the game is amazing. 

I love being able to figure things out by myself and feel somewhat proud that I did it, although it doesn't have the most complicated puzzles, It is super satisfying when you put the pieces together. 

As for the ending, It felt a little rushed, I won't say any spoilers so don't worry, but the ending felt like this happened and then this. It felt all a little sudden, but I presume that's the point. 

While it is a short game, I would say it's worth the money, the graphics are nice and it runs super smooth. I have no complaints. I cannot wait to hear more news on the second game, I will be staying updated, because this my friends... Absolute cinema! 

I literally could not recommend this more, 9/10, point knocked off for being so short. I hope the second game contains more content.

The Good:

- The simulated computer UI is slick and responsive, and very immersive (so long if you suspend disbelief that technology was this advanced in the early 90s lol).
- The soundtrack perfectly sets the mood.
- Most of the connections between clues are interesting and fun to figure out.
- The story is engaging and well-paced.

The Bad:

- The game is too short! Most of my other points are variations of this complaint.
- Not enough cases/clues, so the central mystery builds extremely quickly.
- Some tools you use only once.
- The ending is rather abrupt and either downbeat or an annoying cliffhanger, depending on your perspective.
- Player choice is largely an illusion. Depending on choices, some events play out slightly differently and a tiny bit more of the backstory is revealed or not, but 95% of the story is identical, including the ending.
- Voice acting is fine, but not amazing
- All this feels like a hook for a (hopefully larger and longer) sequel

All in all though, the quality of what IS in the game plus its low price moves it to the recommend column for me. It is up to you if a game you can beat in a sitting or two is worth whatever price it is at the moment. For me, it was.

[h1]Game Review: The Operator[/h1]

[b]Playtime:[/b] 4h
[b]Status:[/b] Completed

The Operator is incredibly fun for its short four-hour runtime.

It is perfect for people who enjoy puzzles and want to feel intelligent while connecting clues. The gameplay is simple, satisfying, and immediately hooks you. The story builds tension well, and the music supports the atmosphere perfectly.

For most of the game, it feels like you have many possible paths.

Unfortunately, that is mostly an illusion.

[spoiler]The story is completely linear, there is only one ending, and it arrives abruptly without a satisfying payoff.[/spoiler]

That leaves a bad aftertaste, even though the four hours before it were great.

[b]7/10 — excellent short-term fun, disappointing ending.[/b]

If you're looking for a game where your choices actually matter, rather than the illusion of choice, I wouldn't recommend this game. No matter what you choose, it all ends the same. And without spoiling anything for anyone that decides to give it a try, the ending isn't great (in my opinion of course). It felt very hopeless and pointless, rather than empowering. This level of inevitability is expected for story mode games like GTA, COD, GOW etc. and I probably would've rated this higher if it shared a similar format. But the choices that weren't really choices is what threw me off. It felt like none of my efforts as a player were rewarded or even mattered at all. Because quite frankly, they didn't. If this game had the option for multiple endings I think it would've been great.

I have depression. Playing games is one of a few ways I try to take my mind off of things that would typically worsen that depression, something that is proving exceptionally more difficult at the time of this writing. I actively avoid media that would obviously worsen that depression. I keep up on my anti-depression meds. This is how I take care of myself.

People are free to enjoy the media that they enjoy, and some people will, and have, really enjoyed this game. I won't fault people for that. As much as I hate to say it, I think I'm probably a case study for why some things need content warnings, because I'm going to be carrying this game's ending with me now and I really wish I didn't have to carry that on top of everything else I deal with on a day-to-day basis.

That said, I will not be directly spoiling anything. I went in blind, which if you're like me, I strongly advise you not to do. Watch a playthrough, or preferably just read up on the community posts first. Those'll mostly tell you all you need to know whether this is a game you'll be able to enjoy or not.

All that aside, the investigative gameplay was great, but a little lacking. They introduce tools and mechanics you use once and never again, which feels like a lot of wasted potential.

Again, if you're like me and prefer to play games to escape having to dwell on all the problems with real life, I advise you to give this game a pass and instead, pick up Scrutinized and play it on Detective Mode. Similar gameplay without reminding you quite as much about how much you really hate some aspects of the world you live in.

I think if I weren't in the mental state I'm in, I probably would have enjoyed the game more, and even appreciated the ending more. It is certainly realistic. It wraps up exactly how I would expect this scenario to end in the real world. I think that's why I hate it. It's just reaffirmation that good things don't actually happen to good people. Something I was already well aware of, and really didn't need a reminder.
